body.statement:
Fix \(b_0>1\).  Suppose that \(\mathcal B_J\) is the normalized local B-spline basis on a quasi-uniform partition and that its degree \(r\) satisfies \(r+1\ge s\) and \(2r+1>\sup_{a\in\mathcal A_{\rm H}}\alpha_a\).  Uniformly over \(P\in\mathcal P_{\rm S}\), heavy arms, fixed folds, and \(\tau\in\mathcal T\), the learner satisfies, up to a fixed power of \(\log n\),
\[
\sup_{d_a(x)\ge n^{-b_0}}
\left|\log\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)-\log\pi_a(x)\right|
=O_P(\delta_{a,n}),
\]
\[
\left|\int m_{a,\tau}(x)
\frac{\widehat\pi_{a,-k}(x)-\pi_a(x)}{\pi_a(x)}\,dP_X(x)\right|
=O_P\!\left(J_n^{-s}+n^{-1/2}J_n^{(\alpha_a-1)/2}
+\frac{J_n^{\alpha_a}}n\right),
\]
and the corresponding relative-error square integral is
\[
O_P\!\left(J_n^{-2s}+\frac{J_n^{\alpha_a}}n\right).
\]
For \(J_n=\lfloor n^\xi\rfloor\) with
\[
\frac1{s(\alpha_a+1)}<\xi<\frac1{\alpha_a+1},
\]
there is a deterministic \(M_n\uparrow\infty\) such that
\[
E_{a,n}M_n^{\gamma_a-1}=o_P(1),
\qquad
\max_{\tau\in\mathcal T}|D_{a,n}(\tau)|=o_P(1).
\]
At \(\alpha_a=s=3/2\) and \(J_n=\lfloor n^{3/10}\rfloor\), the log-error order is \(O_P(n^{-1/8}{\rm polylog}\,n)\), the signed-functional order is \(O_P(n^{-17/40}{\rm polylog}\,n)\), and the normalized interior discrepancy is \(O_P(n^{-1/40}{\rm polylog}\,n)\).
body.justification: This is the early kill test and now derives, rather than assumes, the corrected amplified oracle-transfer condition.
body.gap: Hirano, Imbens, and Ridder control a regular-overlap likelihood projection, not this singular signed Hall-boundary functional.
body.consumer: The lemma supplies a primitive flexible first stage for the non-Gaussian quantile argmin.

obligation.what_is_open: After the necessary dictionary narrowing, prove the uniform constrained Bernoulli likelihood expansion with a random Hessian and the signed weighted functional rate.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen assumptions provide smoothness and Hall tails but no established lower bound for every local Fisher block, no control of the constrained maximizer under separation, and no proof that score cancellation survives the singular log-boundary direction.
obligation.attempted: Derived the Hall normalization, optimized the three claimed error terms, checked the nonempty dimension window, and tested the approximation floor. The degree-zero test gives an explicit counterexample to the unrestricted claim.
obligation.partial_result:
The Hall equation gives
\[
t_{a,n}=(c_an)^{-1/\gamma_a}\{1+o(1)\},
\qquad
h_{a,n}=(c_an)^{1/\gamma_a}\{1+o(1)\},
\qquad
\frac n{h_{a,n}}\asymp n^{1/(\alpha_a+1)}.
\]
Consequently, if the three asserted likelihood bounds are available and \(J_n=n^\xi\), their contributions to the normalized signed discrepancy have respective orders
\[
n^{1/(\alpha_a+1)-s\xi},\qquad
n^{1/(\alpha_a+1)-1/2+\xi(\alpha_a-1)/2},\qquad
n^{1/(\alpha_a+1)-1+\alpha_a\xi}.
\]
All three tend to zero exactly under the displayed sufficient window
\[
\frac1{s(\alpha_a+1)}<\xi<\frac1{\alpha_a+1}.
\]
At \(\alpha_a=s=3/2\) and \(\xi=3/10\), the log rate is \(n^{-1/8}\), the signed rate is \(n^{-17/40}\), and multiplication by \(n/h_{a,n}\asymp n^{2/5}\) gives \(n^{-1/40}\).

The unrestricted frozen claim is nevertheless false.  It permits \(r=0\).  For a degree-zero quasi-uniform spline space and a smooth \(g\) with derivative nonzero on a fixed interior interval, the best uniform approximation error is bounded below by \(cJ^{-1}\).  Choose \(s>(\alpha_a+3)/(\alpha_a+1)\) and
\[
\frac1{s(\alpha_a+1)}<\xi<\frac1{\alpha_a+3}.
\]
Then \(J_n^{-s}+\{J_n^{\alpha_a+1}/n\}^{1/2}=o(J_n^{-1})\), contradicting the asserted log-error rate already at the population approximation level.  This proves the necessity of narrowing the dictionary and degree.  What remains unproved after that narrowing is the constrained random-Hessian expansion producing the signed, rather than absolute, functional rate.
